observations.statement: LSPS-041 is an accepted remote-identity requirement that preserves user-visible SSH and path authority plus host/server/root session keys while forbidding hidden mirrors, silent retargeting, and host-local URI collisions.

LSPS-042 is GUI-related and specifies visible connection-loss controls and copy, offline work only with a validated cache, system keychain or agent credential handling, and consumption of the SSH owner contract.

LSPS-043 is GUI-related and requires preview confirmation for rename, broad format, and multi-file code actions, per-file reporting on partial failures, explicit remote availability modes, and no silent fallback by adjacent surfaces.
LSPS-044 explicitly excludes browser-preview and recover-unsaved residue from LSP wording and places those concerns outside the LSP session key.
LSPS-045 fixes the LSP client and registry in the editor crate under src/lsp, enumerates module files and lsp-types plus tokio, and makes tower-lsp conditional on implementing a server.
LSPS-046 preserves three conceptual structures and names fields spanning identity, lifecycle, freshness, health, enablement, capability, restart, error, document path/version, and attached servers.
LSPS-047 names lifecycle states, a lower-level transition sequence, a three-attempt exponential backoff, 512MB and 30s limits, and restricts normal feature traffic to Ready.
The repeated acceptance pattern is plan-migration traceability and addressability, explicitly creates no executable build work, and names only migration and plan-index validation surfaces.
Every core PlanUnit declares empty dependency and unblock lists even though several units preserve cross-document ContractRefs.

candidate_findings.title: Behavioral acceptance has no executable oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The core acceptance criteria prove source preservation, PlanUnit addressability, and traceability and prohibit creating build work, while the listed validators cover migration and indexing; no runtime, protocol, GUI, failure-injection, or resource-limit acceptance oracle is specified for the required behaviors.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can satisfy every stated validation surface while remote mapping, outage UX, mutation safety, lifecycle transitions, and limits remain behaviorally incorrect.

candidate_findings.title: Projection fields lack type and invariant contracts
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-046 names LspSessionKey, LspSessionProjection, DocumentBinding, and their fields, but the core supplies no field types, nullability, cardinality, value domains, defaults, cross-field invariants, serialization form, update authority, or persistence semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent builders can produce incompatible keys and projections, disagree on requested versus effective enablement and restart/error state, and attach documents to servers inconsistently.

candidate_findings.title: Lifecycle vocabularies do not form a complete state machine
candidate_findings.statement: The canonical lifecycle claim is backed by title-cased user states and a lower-case transition sequence, but RestartBackoff appears only in the former, crashed only in the latter, and ShuttingDown and stopping use different names; no restart edge, allowed-transition table, or terminal outcome is defined.
candidate_findings.impact: Runtime and GUI projections can disagree on legal states and transitions, especially after crashes, during backoff, and while shutting down.

candidate_findings.title: Resource limits have values but no enforcement semantics
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-047 preserves 512MB and 30s but does not state what memory is measured, what request work the time limit covers, how limits are observed, or whether breach cancels, kills, degrades, crashes, reports an error, or consumes restart budget.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can enforce materially different safety policies, causing inconsistent availability, error reporting, and recovery under load.

candidate_findings.title: Remote mutation transaction and recovery semantics are absent
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-043 requires preview confirmation and per-file partial-failure results but does not define confirmation cancellation or expiry, edit ordering, atomicity, rollback, retry, idempotency, concurrent-document conflict handling, or the per-file result schema.
candidate_findings.impact: Remote multi-file operations can be duplicated or left partially applied without a deterministic recovery path or sufficient evidence for safe repair.

candidate_findings.title: Remote availability modes lack transition and operation rules
candidate_findings.statement: The core names full_remote_lsp, degraded_remote_diagnostics_only, and remote_edit_no_lsp and forbids silent fallback, but does not define entry and exit criteria, transition triggers, allowed operations in each mode, stale-snapshot policy, pending-sync reconciliation, or how adjacent Search, Problems, buffers, diffs, and Source Control coordinate mode changes.
candidate_findings.impact: The same outage can yield contradictory capabilities and stale data across surfaces, despite each surface claiming not to fall back silently.

candidate_findings.title: Degraded retry and cache gates are only named
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-042 mentions a validated cache and preserves one-auto-retry, but the core does not bind the retry token to a trigger, timing, credential outcome, cancellation rule, or terminal state, and it does not define cache validation, freshness, invalidation, or allowed offline operations.
candidate_findings.impact: Connection-loss behavior can retry unpredictably or expose stale remote content as safe offline work.

candidate_findings.title: Remote identity and path mapping lack canonicalization rules
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-041 defines host-scoped mapping, a host/server/root key, and collision prohibitions but gives no normalization or validation algorithm for remote paths and URIs, no case or alias handling, and no conflict or error behavior when mappings collide or retargeting is requested.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent paths can form duplicate sessions or edits can be routed to the wrong host or root despite the stated collision prohibition.

candidate_findings.title: Cross-document owner contracts are not dependency edges
candidate_findings.statement: All seven core units leave depends_on and unblocks empty while preserving ContractRefs to FileManager, storage, GitHub Integration, and FinalGUISpec and asserting owner-boundary consumption.
candidate_findings.impact: Planning and build sequencing cannot mechanically require the owner contracts whose vocabulary and behavior these units consume.

candidate_findings.title: GUI metadata excludes user-visible lifecycle obligations
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-041 is marked gui_related false despite user-visible SSH authority and a visible risk reason, and LSPS-047 is marked false despite canonical user/state names and recovery-status exposure.
candidate_findings.impact: GUI planning, coverage, and validation can omit visible identity, risk, lifecycle, degraded, and recovery behavior.

candidate_findings.title: GUI outage and mutation accessibility is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The GUI-related degraded and mutation units require visible status, controls, preview confirmation, and partial-failure reporting but specify no keyboard behavior, focus movement, accessible naming, status announcement, or assistive-technology presentation.
candidate_findings.impact: Users relying on non-pointer or assistive interaction may not perceive or safely control connection recovery and remote edits.

candidate_findings.title: Recovery exclusion names an owner not preserved as a ContractRef
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-044 assigns browser-panel tokens to FileManager, FinalGUISpec, or storage cleanup and recover-unsaved to an editor/storage recovery contract, but its preserved ContractRefs omit FinalGUISpec and do not identify a precise editor recovery contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can agree that recovery is outside LSP yet still lack a mechanically traceable authoritative owner for the excluded behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Module names do not define integration boundaries
candidate_findings.statement: LSPS-045 fixes crate placement, filenames, and dependencies but leaves module responsibilities, public APIs, ownership of mutable state, async task and channel boundaries, cancellation, and error propagation to builders.
candidate_findings.impact: The required layout can be implemented with incompatible concurrency and ownership models that are difficult to integrate or test.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The remote session key explicitly includes host_id, server_id, and root_identity, and hidden mirrors, silent retargeting, and host-local URI collisions are expressly prohibited.

Connection-loss GUI truth includes Connection lost, Reconnect, and offline work gated by a validated cache, while SSH surfaces are explicitly consumers rather than redefinitions of the owner contract.
Preview confirmation, per-file partial-failure reporting, explicit degraded modes, and the prohibition on silent local Git fallback are all stated.
Browser-preview compatibility residue and recover-unsaved behavior are expressly excluded from LSP wording and the LSP session key.
The client crate location, src/lsp file set, lsp-types and tokio dependencies, and the condition under which tower-lsp becomes relevant are explicit.
The projection names and field identifiers are explicit even though their semantic types and invariants are not.
The retry count, backoff durations, memory amount, request duration, and Ready-only normal-traffic constraint are numerically or behaviorally explicit.
The planning scope explicitly prevents creation of WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks.

unknowns.statement: The canonical remote-path and URI normalization, validation, mapping-conflict, and collision-reporting rules cannot be determined from the core.
The definition, freshness threshold, invalidation authority, and permitted operation set for a validated offline cache are unknown.
The trigger, timing, credential-failure interaction, cancellation, and exhaustion outcome of one-auto-retry are unknown.
The transaction, rollback, retry, idempotency, concurrency, and per-file result contracts for remote mutations are unknown.
The entry and exit conditions and precise capability matrix for full, diagnostics-only, and no-LSP remote modes are unknown.
The exact authoritative contract and API for recover-unsaved editor or storage recovery cannot be identified from LSPS-044's preserved ContractRefs.
The public interfaces, async ownership, cancellation, and error propagation among the named src/lsp modules are unknown.
Field types, defaults, optionality, cardinality, serialization, persistence, update authority, and consumers for the three conceptual data structures are unknown.
The complete legal transition graph, restart edge, attempt reset rule, manual-restart behavior, and post-exhaustion state are unknown.
The measurement and enforcement mechanism and user-visible aftermath for the 512MB and 30s limits are unknown.
Keyboard, focus, naming, announcement, and assistive-technology behavior for connection-loss and mutation GUI states are unknown.
The substantive contents of the preserved external ContractRefs cannot be determined under this blind window scope.
No runtime or GUI acceptance receipt for any core behavior can be identified from the stated acceptance criteria and validation surfaces.
